correctness.rationale: Exact independent-set partition gives the corona polynomial factorization. For any real a>=1/4 and integer m>=1, the scalar roots start near -1 at a large and cannot cross iR: imaginary-axis phase equation m theta=3pi/2+2kpi and a=sin(theta)cos(theta)^(m-1), which is <1/4 for m<=6 by explicit angles and for m>=7 by universal maximum sqrt(6^6/7^7)<1/4. Characteristic polynomial recurrence yields base roots of paths and cycles strictly <=-1/4. Supporting exact rational Hurwitz checks (60) and combinatorial checks (19) re-executed from standalone source; finite checks are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The uniform scalar zero-crossing lemma converts any suitably real-rooted base graph into a strictly Hurwitz-stable arbitrary-multileaf corona, yielding novel explicit families of trees with unbounded numbers of branching hubs and cycle-based graphs. This extends stability knowledge beyond spider (one branching hub) families and beyond known single-leaf operation, with an all-parameter algebraic certificate. Not claimed as classification of all stable trees or optimal scalar threshold.
